P1.evidence: The application was acknowledged at the open — 'I already saw a little bit in your application. I just want you to walk me through it' — and then genuinely used three times during the call, including the read-back that produced the most important disclosure ('I saw in your application that you have like lower back pain, right?'). The frame carried two of four parts and was noticeably lighter than usual: 'just have a normal conversation. Go over where you're at at the moment, where you want to go.' No agreement was sought, because the prospect cut straight in with a price demand before the frame could close, and the rep never came back to re-establish it. The open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: The injury check was the one thing this call did well. Prompted by the application, the rep asked about the lower back and then qualified its severity properly — 'on a scale from one to ten, or one is like, ah, it's annoying but it doesn't really bother you too much' — which turned a form-field entry into the material fact of the call: a back that locks up overnight and monthly muscle activation therapy. Current training was established. Everything else was thin or absent. Age, height and weight were never asked, which is remarkable on a call where the stated goal is to put on weight. Occupation was never asked despite being visible in his display name. Health conditions were never asked; the dairy, gluten and peanut exclusions were volunteered. Nutrition got two questions and an eating-window question, then was dropped and never revisited. Sleep and energy were never asked. Twenty minutes is not long, but the phase was truncated because the price conversation consumed the first five.

P3.evidence: The weakest Phase 3 in the batch. Only the surface layer ran: muscle, mobility and a general health question. The bridge was never asked in any form — there is no 'outside of the physical, what's actually driving this', no future-self question, no who-else-does-this-impact, no drive-through and no reflect-back. The prospect opened a door and it was not walked through: asked what better health looks like he answered 'when I work out, I feel good, right? Mental health, clarity, all that good stuff', and the rep replied 'Makes sense. Okay' and moved to his training history. The nearest thing to a why question is 'why do you feel like now is then the right time for you to do it?', which is a timing check rather than a motivation one. Having conceded the main offer was unaffordable at minute four, the rep appears to have stopped selling and started informing.

P4.evidence: The one phase run properly, and efficiently. Past attempts came out — a virtual trainer until five years ago, meal plans, self-directed training since. What happened was traced precisely: 'I put on like 30 pounds of primarily muscle, and then through work and stress and all those other things, I've lost it over the last few years.' Why it stopped was asked directly and produced three distinct causes: 'I think honestly was expense, I had to cut expense, it was during the pandemic. I also was starting to feel a combinational plateau... and I also moved, changed for my career.' The root-cause question was well constructed as an either-or — 'is that that you just have something that changes from time to time and that you don't need to think about programming yourself? Or is it more so that you need to be held accountable?' — and the prospect named the gap himself: 'it's a little bit of both... having a specific plan designed to my body type and what I'm trying to achieve and how I'm progressing or plateauing.' The rep also tested recurrence sensibly: 'if the same thing would come back, then it would just cut you a second time.'

P5.evidence: Effectively absent. The only settle-adjacent move was 'are you also ready to then keep it going, or do you want to let it fall off again?', answered 'No, keep it going', which tests durability rather than making the cost of inaction real. No two-year question, no why-not, no line in the sand. The material was sitting there untouched: he has already run this exact loop once, gained 30 lb of muscle and lost all of it, and has a back that locks up every night. Nothing was made of either.

P6.evidence: Not attempted in any form. No belief question, no going-all-in question, and no yes of any kind was sought at any point. After presenting the one-to-one the rep asked only 'well, what's your thoughts on that?', which drew 'no real questions just yet. I think I need to just see more.' The call then ended with materials being offered. This is the second consecutive call in this batch with no commitment check whatsoever.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted, so the phase drops out of the denominator. Prices were recited as information rather than presented as an offer, no ask was made, and the call closed on 'if you feel like, yeah, this is what I want to do, then come back to me and we'll get you started.'

objection_plays.detail: The money objection arrived first, before discovery, and the play was not run at any point. The rep attempted to reverse the question — 'Is that because you have like a small budget for yourself? ... what is sort of your budget looking like?' — which is not an OC move and which the prospect declined. He then disclosed a range, accepted the prospect's self-set $200-300 a month anchor without challenge, and conceded within four minutes: 'that sounds like that's quite out of what you would want to spend.' No isolation, no should-I-versus-how frame, no offer to explore making it work, and none of the six financial-picture questions. The prospect had just told him he pays a muscle activation therapist monthly and previously paid a virtual trainer for long enough to gain 30 lb — evidence of willingness to pay that was never tested.

Script gap and the one that shaped this call: a prospect who demands the price before discovery. 'Before we go too deep... I want to know what the payment structure... before we spend too much time on this call, just out of respect to each other's time.' There is no scripted move for this — no bridge back to the frame, no reason-why for sequencing discovery first — and the rep complied. Everything downstream followed: Phase 3 collapsed, Phase 5 never ran, and the offer was pre-disqualified against a number set before any value existed. This is the second call in three days where a rep tried to extract the prospect's budget first and it failed; a scripted response is needed.

Second gap: an objection to the delivery format. 'I am a little hesitant about it 99% being text message... is that the right fit?' — from a prospect who has done virtual coaching before and knows from experience that some things need a conversation. No play covers this and the rep's answer effectively handed him the exit: 'it comes down eventually to yourself. Like if you've got a no[gging feeling] I would suggest don't do it then.' The objection was live and unresolved when the call ended.

Third gap: a prospect who distrusts the personalisation claim itself, having bought it before. 'It's sold as it's detailed and tailored, and the reality, it's not the quality or the tailored approach that I would want or need.' This attacks the core of what is being sold and it was not answered — no evidence, no example, no differentiation from what he bought last time, and the nutrition pillar that his complaint was specifically about was never presented at all.

notes: A twenty-minute call in which the prospect set the agenda in the first sixty seconds and the process never recovered. Phase 4 was good; Phases 3, 5 and 6 did not happen. The single coachable moment is the opening: when a prospect asks for the price before discovery, there needs to be a scripted way to acknowledge it, give a reason for sequencing and get back to the frame, because conceding the number early against a self-set budget ended the sale before any value was built. Two things to escalate rather than coach: the price recital included a three-month $4,000 tier and an $8,000 upper bound that are not in the stated offer, and the rep disclosed in passing that pre-call nurture videos are sent by a bot persona the prospect was never told about.
